text.p: Italian bond futures held to firmer levels helped by an early boost from a European stability pact and support from many other bond markets, but the market showed nervousness at the higher levels, dealers said,

An accord between European Union leaders in Dublin over the weekend on a mechanism for ensuing monetary discipline after the launch of a single currency in 1999 boosted the market early, but futures then drifted off the day's best levels.
"We saw a strong mark up early, but the enthusiasm was not there to hold such levels as Italy still has a long way to go to join a single currency," said one dealer on the LIFFE market.

Dealers point out that many operators were likely to remain cautious ahead of preliminary December consumer price index (CPI) inflation figures later this month, when many investors hope a further fall in inflation will prompt the Bank of Italy towards lowering interest rates for the third time this year.
"The market is looking for a CPI rate below November's 2.6 percent which will again help to add pressure for lower interest rates," said the LIFFE trader.
Some dealers added that bond markets were also a little nervous ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOCM) which sets U.S. interest rates.

The lira gained, along with the dollar, helping to give support to contracts, but some investors were troubled by domestic factors such as continued negotiations on Italian engineering and metalworkers' wage contracts.
